name: Asakusa Station
description: Begin at Tokyo Metro Asakusa Station. Check your map, start your recording, and head toward Kaminarimon Gate.

name: Kaminarimon Gate
description: This iconic Thunder Gate marks the entrance to Sensō-ji. Look for its huge red lantern and guardian figures representing thunder and wind.

name: Nakamise and Sensō-ji
description: Walk along Nakamise shopping street toward Sensō-ji, one of Tokyo’s best-known Buddhist temples. Look for the enormous temple gates, five-story pagoda, and main hall.

name: Sumida River / Skytree
description: Stop beside the Sumida River for a clear view of the Tokyo Skytree. This is a strong contrast with the old temple neighborhood.

name: Kappabashi Kitchen Town
description: A traditional district known for restaurant supplies, knives, tableware, and remarkably realistic food models.

name: Tokyo National Museum
description: The Tokyo National Museum preserves and exhibits Japanese and Asian art and cultural objects. The exterior and entrance are worthwhile photo stops even without going inside.

name: Ueno Park
description: Ueno Park brings together tree-lined paths, museums, public art, and open plazas. Pause at the fountain plaza for photographs.

name: Kan’ei-ji Pagoda
description: The five-story pagoda is part of the surviving historic Kan’ei-ji temple complex in Ueno.

name: Ueno Tōshō-gū
description: This Shinto shrine honors Tokugawa Ieyasu. Look for its elaborate gold decoration and impressive entrance.

name: Shinobazu Pond / Bentendō
description: A temple on an island in Shinobazu Pond. Enjoy the waterside views; nearby buildings include a hall dedicated to Daikokuten.

name: Ameyoko Market
description: Explore the shopping alleys and food stalls near the railway tracks. This market district grew rapidly in the years after World War II.

name: Ueno Station
description: Your walk ends at Ueno Station. Review your distance and photos before leaving.
